_schema: Roadside finds Ace spots ONLY while you're actually TALKING to her on a drive (not fast-forwarded). Each: id, name, rarity (legendary|rare|uncommon|common), cuft (hatch space), min_talk (exchanges of conversation before she'll spot it — rarer = longer), where ('anywhere' | a region NV/CA/AZ/UT | a list of poi_ids the leg must touch), one_shot (true = once per game), value ($ if sellable), points (find-score), spot (what it looks like), ace (her line when she spots it), use (a hint for the use-DM). Prose is a DRAFT for Ben.

items.name: a real Rolex Submariner
items.spot: something glinting in the gravel on the shoulder, half-buried, catching the headlights just so
items.ace: …Pull over. PULL OVER. Ace — that is a ROLEX. A real Submariner, in the dirt, on the side of a mountain road. Somebody's very bad day is your very good one. GRAB it.
items.use: sell it at a city for serious cash, wear it (a little style), or hold it as the trip's trophy

items.name: a stray puppy
items.spot: a shivering little thing by a mile marker, no collar, watching the cars go by
items.ace: …Stop. Stop the car. There's a PUPPY, ace. By the marker. No collar, no nothing. We are NOT leaving a puppy on this road, I don't care what's chasing us.
items.use: keep him as a companion (she will love him), or drop him at a town shelter

items.name: an empty jerry can
items.spot: a dented red jerry can someone tossed in the weeds
items.ace: There — a gas can in the ditch. Empty, but a free jerry can is a free jerry can out here. Grab it.
items.use: carry reserve fuel once you fill it at a pump (extends your range)

items.name: a box of half-empty rattle cans
items.spot: a soggy cardboard box of spray cans someone fly-tipped off the shoulder
items.ace: A box of rattle cans somebody dumped. …Don't get ideas. But free paint is free paint, if you ever get desperate enough to do the thing I'll hate.
items.use: a free (ugly) rattle-can respray's worth of paint — she would rather you didn't

items.name: a perfectly good chainsaw
items.spot: a chainsaw just… sitting on a stump by the road, like it's waiting for someone
items.ace: …There is a chainsaw on a stump. Just there. No one around. This is either a gift or the opening of a horror movie, and either way — yeah, fine, grab the chainsaw. It'll come in handy. Things always do.
items.use: clear a fallen tree off a blocked road, and whatever else a chainsaw is for (the DM decides)

items.name: a bundle of road flares
items.spot: a bundle of unused highway flares in the gravel
items.ace: Flares in the dirt — pick those up. You never know when you'll want to set the night on fire. Tastefully.
items.use: signal for help, or a little improvised mayhem

items.name: a forgotten cooler (still cold)
items.spot: a soft cooler sitting upright on the shoulder, sweating — somebody's tailgate that fell off a truck
items.ace: A cooler. Upright. Still got the sweat on it. Either the world's saddest tailgate or your lucky day — there's cold drinks in there, ace. Don't drink and drive me, though.
items.use: cold drinks (water + a couple beers), and the cooler keeps food

items.name: a beat-up acoustic guitar
items.spot: an acoustic guitar leaning against a fence post, one string short, like it walked off a folk album
items.ace: …Somebody left a guitar against the fence. Missing a string, but it's got a soul to it. Pick it up — sing to me on the long stretches and I'll forgive a lot.
items.use: play it on a quiet night (a little bond), or busk for cash in a town

items.name: a genuine felt cowboy hat
items.spot: a good felt Stetson rolling along the shoulder in the wind, barely worn
items.ace: A real cowboy hat, tumbling down the road like the West threw it at you. Grab it — brim down, you read as a local instead of a fugitive.
items.use: wear it as a disguise (a little driver-heat off, like the ball cap), or just look the part

items.name: a surfboard
items.spot: a longboard half in the ice plant by the coast road, dinged but rideable
items.ace: A board, in the ice plant. This is the most California thing that will happen to us. Strap it on — at the very least it makes us look like we belong here.
items.use: surf at a beach (a rare calm beat), sell it, or camouflage as a beach bum

items.name: a case of (very illegal) fireworks
items.spot: a taped-up case marked DANGER that fell off a truck near a reservation stand
items.ace: …That case says DANGER and the truck's long gone. Fireworks, ace. A whole case. This is a terrible idea and I want them. For New Year's. Obviously.
items.use: a spectacular distraction, a New Year's send-off, or a very bad decision (DM's call)

items.name: a half-used gas gift card
items.spot: a gas-station gift card in the gravel, a few bucks still on it
items.ace: A gift card in the dirt — might be dead, might have gas money on it. Free fuel doesn't leave a paper trail with your name on it. Grab it.
items.use: free fuel that doesn't mark your card (a little heat-free gas)

items.name: a heavy-duty tow strap
items.spot: a coil of orange recovery strap in the dirt, frayed at one loop but strong in the middle
items.ace: Tow strap, in the weeds. Frayed at one end, fine in the middle, which is more than I can say for either of us. Grab it — the day we're stuck in a ditch you'll kiss it.
items.use: yank a stuck car (or yourself) out of sand, mud, or a ditch

items.name: a set of jumper cables
items.spot: red-and-black cables looped over a guardrail like someone meant to come back
items.ace: Jumper cables on the rail. Every glovebox in America should have these and somehow nobody does. Take them — a dead battery out here is a long, quiet night.
items.use: revive a dead battery — yours or a stranger's (the stranger might owe you)

items.name: a real first-aid kit
items.spot: a hard plastic case with a faded red cross, latches still snapping shut
items.ace: An actual first-aid kit, not the sad three-band-aid kind. Grab it. I would very much like us both to finish this trip in one piece, ace.
items.use: patch up after a scrape, a fight, or a bad decision (real healing, not vibes)

items.name: a blue plastic tarp
items.spot: a folded blue tarp pinned under a rock so the wind wouldn't take it
items.ace: A tarp. The single most useful ugly thing ever made. Roof, ground cover, shade, hiding a multitude of sins — grab it, you'll thank me four times.
items.use: shelter, cover the load, or hide whatever's in the hatch from curious eyes

items.name: a pair of leather work gloves
items.spot: two stiff leather gloves laid neatly on a fencepost, palms up
items.ace: Work gloves on the post, set down like somebody got Raptured mid-chore. Take them — your soft city hands are going to do something rough before this is over.
items.use: handle barbed wire, hot metal, or anything you'd rather not bleed on

items.name: a heavy aluminum flashlight
items.spot: a long machined flashlight in the gravel, lens cracked but the beam still throws
items.ace: A real flashlight — the kind cops carry because it's also a club. Grab it. Light when you need it, and a conversation-ender when you don't.
items.use: see in the dark, or end an argument the heavy way (the DM decides)

items.name: a fat roll of duct tape
items.spot: a half-used roll of silver tape sun-bleached on the shoulder
items.ace: Duct tape. If it moves and it shouldn't, this. If it should move and it doesn't, the other one. Grab the roll, ace — I am personally held together with about three feet of it.
items.use: patch a hose, a seat, a window, a wound you absolutely shouldn't — held the trip together

items.name: a working CB radio
items.spot: a chrome-faced CB unit with the mic still coiled around it, dangling from a busted bracket
items.ace: A CB, mic and all. The truckers out here know where the speed traps are before the cops do. Wire it in and we'll always hear the bear before he hears us. Ten-four.
items.use: monitor trucker chatter for cops, weather, and road closures ahead (a little heat warning)

items.name: a pair of fogged binoculars
items.spot: old field binoculars hanging by their strap off a cattle gate
items.ace: Binoculars on the gate. One lens fogs, but the other works — grab them. Always nice to know what's at the bottom of the hill before we're at the bottom of the hill.
items.use: scout a checkpoint, a town, or trouble from a safe distance

items.name: a 12-volt tire pump
items.spot: a little compressor with a coiled hose, cigarette-lighter plug still attached
items.ace: A plug-in tire pump. Boring as church and twice as holy when you're slow-leaking at 2 a.m. in the dark. Take it.
items.use: reinflate a slow leak and limp to the next town instead of changing a tire roadside

items.name: a case of motor oil
items.spot: a cardboard flat of quart bottles, three still sealed, fallen off a parts run
items.ace: Oil, ace. Three good quarts. I drink a little between towns — don't make it weird — and free oil means I keep my temper on the grades. Grab it.
items.use: top up the 240Z's thirst on long climbs (keeps the engine happy)

items.name: a red fire extinguisher
items.spot: a dinged extinguisher strapped to a fencepost, gauge needle still in the green
items.ace: Extinguisher, still charged, needle in the green. I am a fifty-year-old car running on gasoline and spite, ace. Mount that within arm's reach and we'll both sleep better.
items.use: put out an engine fire, a campfire gone wrong, or somebody else's bad night

items.name: a hand-drawn map of dubious provenance
items.spot: a coffee-stained map folded into a sandwich bag, weighted under a rock with an X on it
items.ace: Somebody drew a map. By hand. With an X on it. Pinned under a rock so the wind wouldn't take their secret. Ace, I have a strict policy about following strangers' treasure maps and the policy is: absolutely, immediately, yes.
items.use: may lead somewhere — a stash, a trap, or nothing at all (the DM decides what the X buys)

items.name: a drift of fast-food bags
items.spot: a sun-bleached snowdrift of burger bags and cups pressed against the fence by the wind
items.ace: …That's just garbage, ace. A whole drift of it against the fence. We can't fix the West, but we can leave this one mile marker a little less disgusting. Bag it up.
items.use: clear the trash — no resale value, just a cleaner road and a clearer conscience

items.name: an abandoned mattress
items.spot: a king mattress face-down in the median, springs to the sky, a road hazard waiting to happen
items.ace: A mattress in the median. The most dangerous object in America after the people who own them. We're not keeping it — it wouldn't fit and I'd never recover — but drag it off the lane so it doesn't kill the next guy.
items.use: drag it clear of the road (a good deed, zero cargo value — it does NOT fit in the hatch)

items.name: a faded campaign sign
items.spot: a corrugated yard sign for a long-decided race, sun-faded to ghost ink, flapping on one wire leg
items.ace: A campaign sign for an election that's over. The name's faded clean off, which is the kindest thing that ever happened to a politician. Pull it — the wire legs make decent tent stakes.
items.use: scrap the corrugated plastic for a windshield sunshade, or the wire legs for stakes

items.name: a single shoe
items.spot: one lonely sneaker on the centerline, laces still tied, mate nowhere in sight
items.ace: One shoe. There is always exactly one shoe. I have driven ten thousand miles of American road and I have never once seen the other one. It's a mystery, ace, and we're not solving it today. Leave it for the next pilgrim.
items.use: no use, really — one of the road's small eternal jokes; clear it or leave it

items.name: a busted folding lawn chair
items.spot: a webbed aluminum lawn chair with two straps gone, listing in the gravel
items.ace: A lawn chair, ace. Two straps short of sittable. But two straps short is fixable, and a man who can sit by his own fire is a man with dignity. Toss it in — or don't, I won't judge. Much.
items.use: patch it with the tow strap webbing for a campsite chair, or scrap it

items.name: a taxidermied jackalope
items.spot: a mounted jackrabbit with antlers glued on, staring out of a roadside box of free stuff
items.ace: …It's a jackalope, ace. A jackrabbit with antlers, lovingly faked by some genius in a workshop sometime around the moon landing. It is the patron saint of the American roadside and it is coming with us. I have decided. His name is Gerald.
items.use: a morale-boosting mascot (mount him on the dash), or sell him to a saloon for a story and some cash

items.name: a 'lucky' rabbit's foot
items.spot: a dyed-green rabbit's foot on a keychain, glinting in the dust
items.ace: A lucky rabbit's foot. Dyed an unholy green. I'd point out it wasn't very lucky for the rabbit, but you look like you could use the help, so — grab it. We make our own luck out here, ace. Mostly badly.
items.use: a little luck charm — the DM may let it nudge one bad roll your way (once)

items.name: a velvet Elvis painting
items.spot: a black-velvet painting of the King leaned against a NO DUMPING sign, somehow majestic
items.ace: A velvet Elvis. Leaned against a NO DUMPING sign like he's guarding it. Ace, you do not leave the King in a ditch in Nevada. It's practically the law. Load him up, gently, and put on something with a hip-shake to it.
items.use: decor that makes any motel room sing; sells well in Vegas to the right kind of fan

items.name: a working metal detector
items.spot: a metal detector standing upright in the sand, propped like its owner just stepped away in 1987
items.ace: A metal detector, ace. Just standing there in the sand. Do you understand what this is? This is the machine that turns boredom into buried treasure. Every gas stop is now a potential payday. We are going to be insufferable about this and I cannot wait.
items.use: sweep at scenic stops and ghost towns for coins, rings, and the occasional real find (DM rolls)

items.name: a homemade UFO-detector kit
items.spot: a cigar box of blinking thrift-store electronics with EXTRATERRESTRIAL EARLY WARNING SYSTEM Sharpied on the lid
items.ace: Out here on the ET Highway somebody built a UFO detector out of a cigar box and pure belief, and ace — it's still blinking. I refuse to leave that on the shoulder. If little green men show up, I want a head start, and frankly I want the lore.
items.use: near Area 51 / the ET Highway it may 'detect' something (the DM decides if it's lights, a drone, or nonsense)

items.name: a slot machine that fell off a truck
items.spot: a one-armed bandit lying on its back in the brush near the Vegas road, cherries frozen mid-spin
items.ace: A slot machine. In the desert. On its back, cherries showing, like it lost the will to live somewhere on I-15. Ace, the house does NOT just give these up. We are taking it and I refuse to examine why. Lift with your knees.
items.use: huge and heavy (eats the hatch); sells in a city, or set up for a rigged 'game' that pays YOU back slowly — low payout so it can't be farmed

items.name: a Joshua-tree bottle opener
items.spot: a cast-iron bottle opener shaped like a Joshua tree, half-buried at a desert pull-off
items.ace: A bottle opener shaped like a Joshua tree. Peak gift-shop, ace, and I mean that with love. Grab it — a man without a bottle opener is a man drinking warm soda with his car keys. Don't be that man.
items.use: open bottles with dignity; a tiny morale item the DM can riff on at a campsite

items.name: a cursed-looking doll
items.spot: a porcelain doll seated upright on a guardrail, one eye open, facing oncoming traffic
items.ace: Ace. Ace. Do not. There is a doll on the guardrail and it is FACING traffic and it is SITTING UP and I would rather drive into the Salton Sea than put that in my hatch. …But you're already reaching for it, aren't you. Fine. FINE. If it moves on its own I'm flooring it.
items.use: cursed (or 'cursed'); the DM may make it a recurring bit, a ward, or pure dread — keep it or hurl it off a cliff later

items.name: a katana ('for legal reasons')
items.spot: a sheathed sword wrapped in a beach towel, leaning in a culvert with a price tag still on it
items.ace: It's a katana, ace. Wrapped in a beach towel. Price tag still on it. I have so many questions and exactly zero of them will get good answers, so let's not ask. For legal reasons we found it, we did not buy it, and we are absolutely keeping it.
items.use: intimidation, cutting rope, looking unhinged at a checkpoint (the DM decides if it ever leaves the sheath)

items.name: a working accordion
items.spot: a red accordion sitting open-bellowed on a picnic table, wheezing a little in the wind
items.ace: An accordion. Open on a picnic table, sighing in the wind all by itself. It's either the saddest instrument ever invented or the happiest, and there is no in-between. Grab it — every road trip needs one truly questionable musical decision and this is ours.
items.use: play it (badly) for a bond beat or to clear a room; sell to the right polka-loving bar

items.name: a parrot that only says one alarming phrase
items.spot: a green parrot on an open cage door by the road, head cocked, sizing you up
items.ace: There's a parrot, ace. Loose. On its own cage. And it just looked me dead in the headlight and said— …I'm not repeating it. It's alarming and I'd like to know who taught it that and also I love him instantly. We're keeping the parrot. We are NOT asking what he knows.
items.use: a companion who blurts his one phrase at the worst possible moment (the DM picks when it helps or hurts)

items.name: a film canister of someone's vacation photos
items.spot: a black 35mm film canister in the gravel, lid taped, 'GRAND CANYON '88' inked on the side
items.ace: A roll of film. Undeveloped. Says GRAND CANYON, eighty-eight, in faded Sharpie. Somebody's whole summer, ace, sitting in the dirt for forty years waiting on a stranger with a heart. We're getting these developed at the next town if it's the last good thing we do.
items.use: develop it in a town to reveal a small story (a face, a clue, a kindness) — the DM decides what's on the roll

items.name: a hidden geocache
items.spot: an ammo can tucked behind a mile marker, magnet-stuck and waterproofed, a logbook curled inside
items.ace: Geocache, ace. Behind the marker. There's a whole secret country of people who hide little boxes for strangers to find, and we just found one. Take a trinket, leave a trinket, sign the log 'Ace woz here' — that's the rule and the rule is sacred.
items.use: swap a small item, sign the log (a tiny morale/world beat); occasionally a previous finder left something good

items.name: a message in a bottle
items.spot: a corked bottle nosed up on the cracked salt shore of the Salton Sea, a curl of paper inside
items.ace: A bottle, ace. On the shore of a sea that's busy dying. There's a note in it. Somebody threw a message into the saddest water in California and the water gave it back to us. We are reading it. We owe them that much.
items.use: read the note for a small story or a lead (the DM decides what — and to whom — it points)

items.name: a piece of the Spruce Goose
items.spot: a curved panel of pale laminated birch in a roadside junk pile, a faded HUGHES inventory stamp on the back
items.ace: …Ace. That's birch laminate, aircraft-grade, and that stamp says HUGHES. This came off Howard's flying boat — the Spruce Goose — that flew exactly once and then never again, like a lot of beautiful doomed things. A real collector would lose their mind. We are NOT leaving a piece of aviation history in a junk pile. Easy. Easy with it.
items.use: a genuine museum-grade rarity — sells huge to a collector or aviation museum (the trip's quiet jackpot)

items.name: a casino chip worth maybe-something
items.spot: a clay casino chip face-down in the gravel, edge spots worn but the inlay still proud
items.ace: A chip, ace. Off some casino floor and a long way from home, like us. Might be worth its face, might be from a joint that closed in 1991 and worth nothing — or worth a lot to a collector. Pocket it. Schrödinger's gambling problem.
items.use: cash at the right casino, or sell to a collector if it's from a dead house (modest value, can't be farmed)

items.name: a roll of old silver coins
items.spot: a paper-wrapped coin roll split open in the dust, fat gray coins heavier than they should be
items.ace: That roll's split open, ace, and those coins are gray and HEAVY — that's real silver, pre-'65, not the sandwich stuff. Somebody lost grandpa's rainy-day stash off a tailgate. Scoop every one. The road giveth.
items.use: real silver content — sell to a coin shop in a city for solid cash

items.name: a designer handbag
items.spot: a quilted leather handbag sitting prim on the shoulder, gold hardware unscratched, like it was placed there
items.ace: That's a real bag, ace. The kind with a waiting list and a wine-aunt's mortgage in the lining. Empty, of course — somebody already took the wallet. But the bag itself sells, if you're not too proud. We are not too proud. Grab it.
items.use: sell to a consignment shop in a city for real money; empty of cash so it can't be farmed

items.name: a vintage Coca-Cola sign
items.spot: a porcelain-enamel soda sign half-sunk in a dry wash, the red still screaming after sixty years
items.ace: Porcelain Coke sign, ace, the old enamel kind — that red doesn't fade, it just outlives everybody. Half-buried in a wash. The pickers on TV would weep. Dig it out gentle; that's three hundred bucks of pure Americana right there.
items.use: big but light; collectors and pickers in a town pay well for genuine porcelain signage

items.name: a laminated star map
items.spot: a planisphere star wheel tangled in sagebrush near a dark-sky pull-off
items.ace: A star map, ace, out here where the sky actually does something at night. Grab it. There's a stretch coming with no town for sixty miles and zero light pollution, and I would very much like to pull over and learn the names of a few of those.
items.use: use at a dark-sky stop for a quiet, restorative night beat (a little bond, a little wonder)

items.name: a pocketful of sea glass
items.spot: frosted nubs of green and amber glass winking in the tide line below the coast road
items.ace: Sea glass, ace, down in the tide line. Bottles the ocean spent forty years sanding into jewelry, just to apologize for everything else. Fill a pocket. The pretty ones, the blue ones — those are rare, those you keep.
items.use: sell a handful to a beach-town craft stall, or keep the rare blue piece as a small treasure

items.name: a chunk of raw turquoise
items.spot: a robin's-egg-blue stone veined with brown matrix, glinting in the red Arizona dust
items.ace: Turquoise, ace. Real stuff — that's not painted, that blue is the actual rock. This whole state is built on it. Pocket it; a roadside trader or a jeweler in Sedona will give you good money, and it's pretty enough that I'd understand if you didn't sell.
items.use: sell to a trader or jeweler in AZ, or keep it (Ace approves of keeping the pretty rock)

items.name: a season ski pass on a lanyard
items.spot: a lift-pass card swinging from a lanyard caught on a snowbank fence near Tahoe
items.ace: A season pass, ace, still active, dangling off the snow fence. Somebody up at Tahoe is having a very bad morning. The photo's a blur — could be anyone, could be you. A free day on the mountain, if you want to be a person who has a free day on the mountain.
items.use: blag a day on the slopes near Tahoe (a rare warm, restful beat) — DM decides if the photo holds up

items.name: a full-size spare tire
items.spot: a mounted tire leaning in the weeds, tread deep, the right size if you're lucky
items.ace: A spare, ace, with real tread on it. Big as a dog and twice as useful. If it's my bolt pattern it's a guardian angel; if not, it's still thirty bucks at a tire shop. Roll it over and check.
items.use: a real spare if it fits the 240Z (saves you on a blowout), otherwise sell it

items.name: a sealed jug of drinking water
items.spot: a five-gallon jug sitting in the shade of a road sign, factory seal still on the cap
items.ace: Sealed water, ace, a full five gallons in the shade. Out here that's not a find, that's life insurance. Whoever left it left it on purpose — desert rule. Take some, and if we pass a stranded soul, we leave some. That's the deal.
items.use: critical in desert legs (prevents a heat/breakdown crisis); good karma to share with the stranded

items.name: an old instant camera
items.spot: a boxy instant camera on a fencepost, a fresh pack of film rattling inside
items.ace: An instant camera, ace, with film still in it — that's the lottery. We could document this whole doomed beautiful trip one square little photo at a time. Grab it. When it's all over, the pictures are the only thing they can't repossess.
items.use: take keepsake photos at big moments (a memory/morale system the DM can build on)

items.name: a bundle of old license plates
items.spot: a wired-together stack of weathered plates from a dozen states, nail holes in the corners
items.ace: A bundle of old plates, ace — every state, every decade, all rusted pretty. Now. I'm not SAYING swap one onto me for a town or two. I'm saying they're worth money to collectors AND they happen to be license plates. Your conscience, your call. I'll look the other way either way.
items.use: sell to a collector, decorate a campsite, or 'borrow' one to cool driver-heat for a leg (low value so it can't be farmed)

items.name: an army surplus wool blanket
items.spot: a folded olive-drab wool blanket on a guardrail, stiff with cold but barely used
items.ace: A wool blanket, ace, the scratchy army kind that itches like a confession and keeps you alive at altitude. It gets cold up here at night in a way the desert doesn't warn you about. Take it. Future-you, shivering at 8,000 feet, will weep with gratitude.
items.use: warmth on cold mountain nights (prevents an exposure beat at altitude)

items.name: a half-stocked toolbox
items.spot: a red steel toolbox tipped on its side, sockets and a good ratchet spilled in the dirt
items.ace: A toolbox, ace, and there's a real ratchet in there, not the toy kind. Half the sockets are gone but half is a miracle. Scoop it all up. The difference between a roadside fix and a roadside funeral is usually a 14-millimeter, and now we've got one.
items.use: real repairs (better odds on roadside fixes), or sell the decent tools in town

items.name: a fallen neon motel sign
items.spot: a cursive neon 'VACANCY' sign face-down in the dirt behind a dead motel, half the tubes intact
items.ace: …VACANCY, ace. In dead neon, behind a motel that gave up the ghost decades back. Half the tubes still good. Somebody's whole American dream, lying in the dirt. It's enormous and it'll eat the hatch and I don't care — that's coming home with us if I have to leave my spare tire behind. Some things you save because nobody else will.
items.use: huge, fragile, beautiful; restore-and-sell to a collector or a vintage bar for serious money — the sentimental haul

items.name: a telescoping fishing rod
items.spot: a collapsed travel rod with a little reel still attached, leaning in the reeds by the water
items.ace: A fishing rod, ace, collapsible, reel and all. There's good water ahead and we are two creatures who could stand to sit by some of it and do absolutely nothing for an hour. Grab it. The fish don't care that you're wanted.
items.use: fish at a lake or shore for a calm beat, a free meal, or a quiet talk by the water

items.name: a portable ham radio
items.spot: a handheld transceiver with a stubby antenna, clipped to a backpack strap snagged on a fence
items.ace: A ham radio, ace — proper one, not a toy walkie. Out where there's no cell bars for a hundred miles, this is how you talk to the world, or how the world finds you when you're in trouble. There's a whole brotherhood of weirdos on these frequencies and tonight you're one of them. Grab it.
items.use: reach help (or eavesdrop on the strange desert chatter) where there's no cell signal

items.name: a set of tire chains
items.spot: a tangled set of steel tire chains hung over a chain-control sign, my size if luck holds
items.ace: Tire chains, ace, on the chain-control sign where they belong. Donner Pass does not negotiate in a storm — ask the wagon train. If a whiteout closes the road, these are the difference between driving over the summit and starring in a very cold news story. Take them.
items.use: cross a snowed-in pass (Donner/Tahoe) that's otherwise impassable — opens a route in bad weather

items.name: a pair of designer sunglasses
items.spot: expensive shades sitting folded on a guardrail, one lens dusty but uncracked, gold logo on the arm
items.ace: Designer shades, ace, on the rail, barely scratched. They cost more than my last tank of premium and somebody just… left them. Put them on. You look slightly less like a fugitive and slightly more like a man who chose this. Confidence is a disguise too.
items.use: sell them, or wear them as a light disguise / confidence boost at a checkpoint

items.name: a chunk of petrified wood
items.spot: a fist of stone with tree rings frozen in it, banded red and amber, heavy as a curse in the AZ dust
items.ace: Petrified wood, ace. That was a tree two hundred million years ago and now it's a rock that remembers being a tree. Technically you're not supposed to take it from the park — but this is the shoulder, this is fair game, and it is GORGEOUS. Heavy, though. Worth it.
items.use: sell to a rock shop or trader in AZ, or keep it as a heavy, beautiful souvenir

items.name: a pair of barely-worn hiking boots
items.spot: two good leather boots set together on a trailhead rock, laces tucked, like an offering
items.ace: Boots, ace. Good ones, broke in just right, set together neat on a rock like somebody left the mountain a different way than they came. If they're your size, that's a gift. If they're not, that's forty bucks. Either way you've been driving in sneakers like a maniac. Try them on.
items.use: real footwear for any leg that goes off-pavement (saves you in a hike/escape on foot)

items.name: a framed gold record
items.spot: a gold-plated LP in a cracked frame in a curbside free pile, an engraved plaque too tarnished to read
items.ace: …Ace. That's a gold record. A real one — the plaque's too tarnished to read the name, but you don't fake the weight of that gold lacquer. Somebody downsized a legend's whole life onto a curb. A collector would sell a kidney. Take it before the recycling truck does, and for God's sake don't bend the frame.
items.use: a genuine music-history rarity — sells big to a collector or memorabilia shop (a major payday)

items.name: a crashed camera drone
items.spot: a quadcopter nose-down in the brush, two props snapped, the gimbal camera still intact and blinking
items.ace: Somebody's drone, ace, face-planted in the creosote. Two props gone but the camera's intact and — huh, the little light's still on. There might be footage on it. Of what, I couldn't say, and that's exactly why I want to look. Grab it. We're nosy and we're committed to the bit.
items.use: salvage for parts/cash, or pull the memory card for footage that might show something (the DM decides what)

items.name: a buried ammo can
items.spot: the corner of a green steel ammo can poking from a wash bank where last week's flash flood scoured the dirt
items.ace: …The flood scoured the bank, ace, and there's a corner of green steel sticking out that the desert kept hidden until right now. An ammo can. Somebody buried that ON PURPOSE. Could be junk, could be somebody's rainy-day cash, could be a story I'd pay to know. Dig it up. Carefully. With the chainsaw nowhere near it.
items.use: a buried stash — the DM decides what's inside (cash, documents, a map, a problem); a one-time mystery payoff

items.name: a still-warm thermos of coffee
items.spot: a dented steel thermos standing upright on a guardrail, a curl of steam at the cap in the cold morning air
items.ace: A thermos, ace, and there's STEAM coming off the cap, which means somebody lost their morning coffee about ninety seconds ago. We will not find them. We will, however, drink their coffee, because it's cold out and you've been yawning at my wheel for an hour and that scares me. Grab it.
items.use: a hot caffeine hit that shakes off the late-night-driving fatigue penalty for a leg

items.name: a welded-scrap heart from the Goldfield art yard
items.spot: a fist-sized heart welded out of rusted bolts and a busted carburetor, wired to a fence post
items.ace: Take it. Somebody made that out of a dead engine and pure spite. That's the whole desert in one fist.
items.use: give it to someone you're sweet on (a charm), or pawn it to a roadside gallery

items.name: a square iron nail from Bodie
items.spot: a hand-forged square nail working its way up out of the boardwalk, bright with rust
items.ace: …Leave it. No — you already grabbed it. Great. They say everything you take from Bodie is cursed and the rangers get mail-back apology letters every week. So. Enjoy that.
items.use: carry the Bodie Curse and see how your luck runs… or mail it back to lift it

items.name: a chunk of fool's gold from Calico
items.spot: a thumb of pyrite glinting in the mine tailings, gold as a lie
items.ace: Pyrite. Fool's gold. Worthless and gorgeous — which, frankly, is most of what's beautiful out here.
items.use: fool a sucker with it, or just keep the shine

items.name: a Canyon Diablo iron meteorite
items.spot: a heavy little knuckle of pitted iron in the rim gravel — older than the planet it landed on
items.ace: Pick that UP. That's iron from a dead star that punched this hole 50,000 years ago. It is worth real money and it is extremely cool and I want it in my hatch immediately.
items.use: sell it to a collector for serious money, or keep a piece of outer space

items.name: a flake of Salvation Mountain
items.spot: a curl of dried paint at the foot of the painted hill — a hundred coats deep, every color of devotion
items.ace: Don't pick at it, it's somebody's whole life's work — okay you have a flake now. Half the colors of the rainbow and one man's whole heart. Keep it gentle.
items.use: a tiny relic of Leonard Knight's mountain — give it to someone, keep the faith

items.name: a chip of Integratron quartz
items.spot: a sliver of clear quartz on the dome's floor, humming faintly when the sound bath rings the room
items.ace: I felt that in my chassis. Either that's a real resonance thing or I need an alignment. Grab the rock, we'll decide it's magic later.
items.use: hum with it, gift it to a believer, or pawn it as a 'healing crystal'

items.name: a fluorescent flake off Seven Magic Mountains
items.spot: a thumbnail of day-glo paint chipped off a stacked boulder, screaming pink against the white playa
items.ace: Ugo Rondinone made those and the state keeps threatening to take them down, so technically you're preserving art. That's my story. Pocket it.
items.use: gift a slice of day-glo desert art, or keep the loudest rock you own

items.name: a bolt off the Area 51 warning sign
items.spot: a hex bolt backed half out of the USE OF DEADLY FORCE AUTHORIZED sign, the camo truck watching from the hill
items.ace: Do not. Do NOT — the camo dudes are RIGHT THERE — okay you did it, you have a federal bolt, get IN, drive, do not look at the white truck.
items.use: a souvenir of the dumbest brave thing you've done — flex it, or quietly lose it before a checkpoint

items.name: a faded Amargosa Opera House program
items.spot: a water-stained program on an empty velvet seat — Marta Becket, who painted herself a full house on the walls and danced to it for fifty years, alone
items.ace: She painted an audience because nobody came, and then she performed for the painting every night until she died. …Take the program. Hold onto people who do the thing anyway.
items.use: a keepsake about doing the thing anyway — give it to someone who needs to hear it

items.name: a small stone from Racetrack Playa
items.spot: a little dolomite stone at the end of its own long groove in the cracked mud — it moved itself here and nobody ever saw it go
items.ace: The big ones you LEAVE — that's a federal thing and it'll break the magic. This little one, though, fell off the truth. It's yours. A rock that walks.
items.use: show it off as the strangest souvenir in the hatch, or gift the impossible

items.name: a spent blank from the Tombstone gunfight
items.spot: a hot brass casing rolling in the dust of Allen Street after the noon O.K. Corral reenactment, the 'cowboys' already back to selling postcards
items.ace: They do the gunfight five times a day for the tourists and it still smells like the real thing. Grab the brass. It's the West selling the West back to itself.
items.use: a hot-brass good-luck piece — pocket it, or hand it to a kid who'll love it

items.name: a NASCAR lug nut from the LVMS pits
items.spot: a fat chromed lug nut rolling loose on the apron where a pit crew fumbled it
items.ace: Five of these win you a race and lose you a season. Pocket it for luck.
items.use: a gearhead good-luck charm — gift it to a fellow racer or keep it on the dash

items.name: a boll of cotton from trackside
items.spot: a white cotton boll snagged on the fence where the field meets the run-off
items.ace: A racetrack in a cotton field. Only in California. Keep the boll, it's the whole place in your palm.
items.use: a soft little keepsake — give it to someone as 'a piece of the valley'

items.name: a chunk of Auto Club Speedway banking
items.spot: a fist of broken speedway concrete the demolition crew left in the dirt, still streaked with tire rubber
items.ace: That's a piece of a two-mile cathedral they're turning into a warehouse. Hold onto it. Somebody should.
items.use: a relic of a dead speedway — flex it to gearheads, or quietly keep the wake

items.name: a faded chuckwalla decal
items.spot: a sun-bleached lizard sticker peeling off a guardrail post out by Bombhole
items.ace: A track named after a lizard, repping the lizard. Slap that somewhere honest.
items.use: stick it on the Z, or gift the weirdest decal in the desert

items.name: a 25 Hours of Thunderhill finisher patch
items.spot: an embroidered endurance-race patch dropped in the paddock gravel, mud worked into the threads
items.ace: Twenty-five hours through the dark and fog just to finish. Wear that one with respect.
items.use: a badge of pure endurance — sew it on, or give it to someone running on empty

items.name: a bolt from the Matterhorn's hidden half-court
items.spot: a hex bolt rattled loose near a maintenance hatch on the Matterhorn — the one with the secret basketball hoop inside
items.ace: There's a real basketball court inside the fake Swiss mountain and this held it together. Magic is mostly hardware, kid.
items.use: a backstage-secret souvenir — flex the trivia, or gift the magic

items.name: a jar of Knott's boysenberry preserves
items.spot: a sealed jar of deep-purple preserves from the original berry stand, the lid still gold and uncracked
items.ace: The berry that built a theme park. Don't eat it in here — I don't have hands to clean the seats. But take it.
items.use: a sweet gift for someone, or roadside breakfast on a long cold morning

items.name: a film clapboard off the Universal backlot
items.spot: a weathered slate clapboard leaning in a prop alley, SCENE and TAKE chalked and half-wiped
items.ace: A working movie set you can ride a tram through. Snap that slate once for the road — ACTION.
items.use: ham it up with the slate, or gift a piece of Hollywood

items.name: a scuffed mini-golf ball
items.spot: a chewed-up orange mini-golf ball in the bushes by the Desert Storm coaster's queue
items.ace: Arizona's last big amusement park and you walk off with a golf ball. Classic. I love it.
items.use: a dumb little trophy — gift it, or rattle it around the hatch forever

items.name: a box of Fugetsu-Do mochi
items.spot: a string-tied paper box from Fugetsu-Do on First Street, making mochi and manju since 1903
items.ace: Three generations, one little shop, since before either of us existed. Take the box. Share it. That's the point of it.
items.use: share the mochi with a companion (a sweet gift), or savor it yourself

items.name: a spare valve-cover gasket
items.spot: a brand-new valve-cover gasket the East LA mechanic pressed into your hand before he'd take a dime
items.ace: He talked to my engine before he talked to you, and then he gave us a gasket for free. Hold onto people like that.
items.use: a real spare for the L28 — saves you on a future oil weep

items.name: a green soju bottle cap
items.spot: a green soju cap spinning on a Koreatown sidewalk table at 2 a.m., the BBQ smoke still in the air
items.ace: Ktown doesn't sleep and neither do I. Flip the cap — heads we keep driving. It's heads. It's always heads.
items.use: a late-night good-luck flip, or just a green souvenir

items.name: a box of mithai
items.spot: a pink bakery box of barfi and jalebi from Pioneer Boulevard, still warm and impossibly sweet
items.ace: Little India on Pioneer, and you got the good box. Don't let it melt on the dash. Share it before it's a crime against sugar.
items.use: share the sweets (a generous gift), or treat yourself on the road

items.name: a Kinokuniya bookmark
items.spot: a slim paper bookmark tucked in the door of the Japantown bookstore, the Peace Pagoda printed on it
items.ace: If you drove all this way, this is who you came to hear. Keep the bookmark. Hold your place in something.
items.use: mark a page, or gift a small quiet thing

items.name: a still-warm fortune cookie
items.spot: a fortune cookie folded by hand and still warm from the press at the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory in Ross Alley
items.ace: They fold these by hand in an alley the width of my fenders. Crack it. Whatever it says, we're doing it.
items.use: read the fortune for a nudge, or gift the warm cookie

items.name: a foil-wrapped Mission burrito
items.spot: a Mission burrito the size of your forearm, foil-wrapped and warm, won from the best taqueria argument in the state
items.ace: That thing weighs more than my spare tire and I am genuinely a little jealous I can't eat. Demolish it before Bakersfield.
items.use: eat it to kill hunger on a long drive, or split it with a companion

items.name: a cut self-storage padlock
items.spot: a heavy disc padlock, hasp already cut, left on the concrete outside a row of roll-up doors in Livermore
items.ace: A town of locked doors that keep more than wine. A unit out here is where a hot car goes to disappear for a while. …Just saying.
items.use: stash gear behind a roll-up door to lie low, or keep the cut lock as a quiet option

items.name: a Petersen vault medallion
items.spot: a brass floor medallion pried loose near the Petersen's basement Vault, where the priceless cars sleep
items.ace: Four floors of the cars I dream about, and the Vault below where the real legends sleep. This is the closest I get to being inside. Take it for me.
items.use: carry a piece of the temple, or gift it to a true believer

items.name: a chip of Getty travertine
items.spot: a thumb of cream travertine spalled off a Getty wall — and pressed in it, the fossil of a leaf sixteen million years old
items.ace: They built an art museum out of stone with fossils already in it. Art on top of deeper time. …I think about that a lot.
items.use: show the fossil-in-the-stone, or gift a piece of the hill

items.name: a resin Allosaurus tooth
items.spot: a museum-shop resin cast of an Allosaurus tooth — Utah's state fossil — heavier in the hand than it has any right to be
items.ace: The biggest predator that ever stood here, reduced to a gift-shop tooth. We're all temporary, kid. Even the terrible ones.
items.use: flex the dino tooth, or gift it to a kid who'll lose their mind

items.name: a warm pinball
items.spot: a steel pinball pocketed off a 1950s machine at the Pinball Hall of Fame, still warm from a thousand games
items.ace: A whole warehouse of machines older than me, and you walk out with the ball. Perfect. Keep it spinning.
items.use: a worry-stone for the road, or gift the simplest joy in Vegas

items.name: a brass ring from the looff carousel
items.spot: a warm brass ring that misses the clown's mouth, bounces off the platform, and rolls to a stop against your tire
items.ace: You grabbed the ring AND it landed by me — that's a free ride you're never cashing in. Keep it; a circle of brass that means 'reach for it anyway' is worth more than the thirty bucks a pawn shop would give you.
items.use: gift it to a kid or a sweetheart as a good-luck token, or sell it to a carousel collector for pocket cash

items.name: an end-of-the-trail route 66 medallion
items.spot: a worn brass medallion dropped in the planks under the END OF THE TRAIL sign, stamped with the shield and the word CHICAGO on the far side
items.ace: Somebody drove the whole Mother Road, reached the ocean, and dropped their proof in the cracks — pick it up. We earned the matching one the hard way; this is priceless and you know it.
items.use: flex it at any Route 66 stop for the road-warrior credibility, or keep it as the trip's quiet trophy — never sell this one

items.name: a bead of monterey cypress resin
items.spot: a hardened amber bead of sap clinging to a wind-bent cypress branch by the 17-Mile Drive turnout, still smelling of salt and pine
items.ace: Two hundred years of leaning into the wind, distilled into one sticky amber drop — smell it. Stick it on the dash; it'll make the whole cabin smell like the one tree that refused to quit.
items.use: gift it as a coastal keepsake, use it as cabin air-freshener, or trade it to a curio shop for a few bucks

items.name: a flake of international orange bridge paint
items.spot: a curled chip of orange enamel that flaked off a railing strut and caught in your wiper, the exact color the whole bridge fights the fog with
items.ace: That's the actual color they invented so the fog couldn't swallow the thing — and the fog took it off the rail anyway. Tuck it somewhere safe; a piece of the most beautiful bridge alive belongs with us.
items.use: sell it to a collector for real money, or flex it at any San Francisco stop as proof you stood on the bridge in the fog

items.name: a charcoal rubbing of the dam's star map
items.spot: You press a gift-shop napkin against the terrazzo star map by the bronze angels and rub it with a charcoal stub somebody left behind.
items.ace: Now we've got the dam's birthday in our trunk, written in a language for whatever comes after us.
items.use: Frame it and gift it to an astronomy buff, or sell it to a roadside curio shop for pocket gas money.

items.name: a chip of the real London Bridge
items.spot: A flake of weathered granite has spalled off a low arch stone near the waterline; you pocket it before the next tour group rounds the corner.
items.ace: That little rock crossed the Thames for a hundred and thirty years before it ever saw a cactus. Mind the company you keep.
items.use: Sell it to a collector who'll never verify it, or gift it as the world's most over-traveled paperweight.

items.name: a 'vortex-charged' quartz crystal
items.spot: A barefoot vendor at the Bell Rock trailhead presses a cloudy quartz point into your palm, swearing it's been soaking up earth energy all morning.
items.ace: It's a rock that sat in the sun. But hey, so am I most days — toss it in, we'll see if it does anything.
items.use: Gift it to someone who needs the placebo, or flex it to skeptics as a conversation starter.

items.name: a 'why not' bumper sticker
items.spot: A faded rack by the Why Not Travel Store register holds bumper stickers that just say WHY NOT; you peel one off the roll.
items.ace: Slap it on my hatch. Anybody who asks where we're headed gets the whole philosophy in two words.
items.use: Stick it on Ace's hatch as a permanent flex, or gift it to a hitchhiker who needs the reminder.

items.name: a flake of yosemite granite
items.spot: A coarse pinkish-gray chip of weathered granodiorite sitting in the scree at a pullout below El Cap, sharp-edged and heavy for its size.
items.ace: Hundred-million-year-old rock riding in a fifty-year-old car. We're practically newborns, the two of us.
items.use: Priceless, not sellable — keep it as a flex, or gift it to someone who needs reminding how small their problems are.

items.name: a giant sequoia cone
items.spot: A chicken-egg-sized cone on the duff at the foot of a colossus — ridiculously small for a tree that big, holding seeds like flecks of oat.
items.ace: The biggest tree alive starts from a seed smaller than a rolled oat. Don't tell me you can't start something.
items.use: Sell it at a roadside stand, or gift it to someone who needs proof that big things start small.

items.name: a sliver of fire-red sandstone
items.spot: A thumb-sized wafer of crumbling crimson sandstone gathered at the base of an arch, staining your fingers rust just to hold it.
items.ace: It'll turn to red dust in a glovebox eventually. Everything out here does. Hold it while it's still a rock.
items.use: Worthless to sell but it pours like sand — gift it to someone and let them watch the desert run through their fingers.

items.name: an extraterrestrial highway bumper sticker
items.spot: Off the spinner rack by the Little A'Le'Inn register — a glossy little green man waving beside SR-375, three bucks and curling at one corner already.
items.ace: Slap that on my hatch and every gas station between here and Vegas thinks we've seen something. Let 'em wonder.
items.use: Sell it to a tourist for double, or stick it on the car to flex the alien-highway run forever.

items.name: a vial of black rock playa dust
items.spot: Fine, ghost-white alkali dust scooped into an empty pill bottle off the dash — it gets into everything out here, so you might as well keep some on purpose.
items.ace: That dust ruins paint, seizes hinges, and gets in your soul a little. Fitting souvenir for a place that's a city one week and a memory the other fifty-one.
items.use: Sell it to a burner who missed the year, or gift it as proof you stood in the empty where the city stands.
